title: The hallmarks of cancer immune evasion
source: Galassi C, Chan TA, Vitale I, Galluzzi L — review
one_line: A review proposing a 'Three Cs' framework — Camouflage, Coercion, Cytoprotection — to organise the mechanisms by which cancer cells evade immune control and the therapies aimed at each.
key_claims: Camouflage covers evasion of detection: MHC class I and B2M/TAP1-2 downregulation, epigenetic silencing of antigen processing genes, impaired chemoattraction (ATP, ANXA1, CXCL10, CCL2), defective CALR-dependent ICD phagocytosis, and physical exclusion by CAFs, TAMs or TANs via TGFβ1 or NETs.

Coercion covers active immunosuppression: immune checkpoint ligands (PD-L1, HLA-E, CD47), defective PRR/DAMP/type I IFN signalling including CGAS-STING and viral mimicry, anti-inflammatory cytokine skewing (CCL2, TGFβ1, CXCL8, IL33 over IFNs and IL1B), and metabolic reshaping of the TME.
Metabolic coercion works both by nutrient depletion (glucose, glutamine, methionine) and by release of immunosuppressive metabolites (adenosine, kynurenine, lactate, TCA byproducts, PGE2).

Cytoprotection covers resistance to killing: altered immunological synapse formation, defective death signalling (CASP8 mutations, FAS downregulation, impaired TNF/IFNG signalling), and compensatory autophagy.

Clinically, approved agents (PD-1/PD-L1, CTLA-4, LAG-3 ICIs, CAR T cells, bispecifics, cytokines) and investigational ones (TIM-3, TIGIT, VISTA, NKG2A, CD47 blockade; metabolic modulators; STING agonists; PRMT5/KDM1A and epigenetic modifiers) can be mapped onto the Three Cs.
limitations: Authors note some immune evasion mechanisms do not fit neatly into the Three Cs categories.
Intratumoral heterogeneity means different tumor regions may rely on different 'Cs', complicating single-target strategies.
Metabolic-pathway therapies currently lack sufficient specificity and efficacy.
Predictive biomarkers beyond PD-L1 expression are largely missing for the newer immunotherapy classes.
As a conceptual review, it presents no new primary data or head-to-head validation of the framework.
open_questions: Which of the three 'Cs' dominates as the driver of resistance in a given tumor, and does targeting the dominant one outperform combination approaches?
Can spatially resolved profiling show that distinct tumor regions use distinct evasion programs, and does that predict therapy failure?
Do biomarkers beyond PD-L1 reliably select patients for checkpoint, metabolic or STING-directed agents?
